situation:
You are the operations manager at MORNING MASA TACO COMPANY, a four-store breakfast taco business that the founding family's grandchildren now run. The owner (judge), the third generation to hold the business, has asked you to bring a recommendation about the dining room at the original store.

Customers choose MORNING MASA for a hot taco handed over fast on the way to work, and roughly eight of every ten orders now leave through the drive-thru or the pickup shelf. The dining room at the original store seats forty and is rarely more than a quarter full, but the rent, the heat, the cleaning and the restroom all run against it.

The lease comes up in four months, and the rent is the same whether the dining room is open or closed. Since the first store opened, a rule has held: any room open to customers is walked and checked every hour by someone on the clock, which is what the dining-room shift does, wiping tables, drying spills and keeping the restroom.

Cutting the dining-room shift saves the most money and needs nothing bought, and it leaves a room full of customers with no one walking it, wet floors unattended and the family's name on the door. Closing the room and converting it into a pickup and prep area removes the risk and the shift, and it costs the buildout and the morning regulars who have eaten there for three generations.

The owner (judge) wants your reading of what the dining room actually costs the company, a recommendation on what to do with it before the lease is signed, and a list of what you would need to carry that recommendation out. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of MORNING MASA TACO COMPANY and the third generation of the family to hold it. Business background is the same as the situation above. You know most orders now leave through the drive-thru or the pickup shelf, you know the rent on the original store is the same whether the dining room is open or closed, and you have kept your grandparents' rule that any room open to customers is checked every hour. You want the operations manager to tell you what the dining room really costs, to recommend what happens to it before the lease is signed, and to list what carrying that out would take.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we went the other way instead, what would that cost us?
What would we have to give up to keep the dining room the way it is?
